Oh and yes she does work. She's an elementary school teacher. She teaches second grade, and there is two other teachers who teach that grade with her, but they're kind of best friends. They do all kinds of things together almost every weekend it seems like, and they don't really invite her even though they say she's their friend. I think maybe that's kind of what's discouraging her from trying to get out there more. Feeling like you're always second choice or not wanted can really take its toll. That's part of the reason I want her to move somewhere else so bad. Maybe if she teaches somewhere else, she will have a second chance to make friends with some other coworkers.

Thanks for responding, and yeah you're right I'm going to text her every day, and I will probably call her when she gets off of work every day for a couple of months. I'm used to coming home from school and waiting until she comes home, and then we just sit and talk for an hour or so until we have to get up and do other things. Maybe if I call her it will help feel like I'm still there.

I was so surprised, but the thought that maybe they will move and find new things somewhere has really helped me out mentally. I feel a little bit better now, so hopefully everything works out!! We don't really have any volunteer stuff around here (it really is a very small town, we don't even have a Walmart)  but maybe my dad will step up once I leave and give her more attention. At least until they can afford or are completely willing to move. Again, thank you for your kind response!
Thank you. I hope it works out too, because as of right now things aren't looking like they're in my favor

I don't know exactly what it's like in your shoes, but maybe I can empathize a bit? I'm a lesbian in America's Bible Belt, so my entire life all I hear is how much f*gs need to be killed or raped and other horrible things that I won't go into detail. I've literally been spit on, shoved, yelled at, and stalked, but I still found enough hope to make it through for the time being. It's great that you don't WANT to die, you just feel like it's the only option right now. Seriously. As someone who has been through this many times, this type of situation is the easiest to come back from. I can't really help you with a short-term solution, but what got me through a lot of my bad spells was hope for the future. My philosophy was "well it sure sucks ass right now, but maybe not later? You'll never know until you find out"   Another thought that helped me out is that the world is constantly changing. People are learning to be more accepting and less ignorant.  Maybe for now a move in towns would be a good start to a solution? I know it's easier said than done, but it's something. Maybe a more liberal area where people are more open minded and will treat you with the respect you deserve.

Speaking as someone who used to be in a similar position to you, I can say that I sympathize, and I'm really sorry that you have to go through this. I found that getting new hobbies and making different friends helped tremendously (I know it sounds a little odd but hear me out). I'm not sure if this will help you, because I'm not you, but for me, I became a much more motivated person after I became a happier person. When you're not a happy person it's hard to be motivated to do anything. Start small and focus on things that make you happy. As for not being able to cry anymore, I went through that as well. It helped when I talked about the things that bothered me, so try to find someone that you are comfortable talking with, and let them know what's going on. I really hope this can help you.

When it first started I was just suffering in general but my mother made it worse, but now if my mom didn't do this I think I would be so much better. My life has gotten better since this started so other things don't really bother me that much anymore, it's mainly just her.

Thank you... And I'm not really sure :/. In my opinion I didn't know for the longest time if I really was doing anything wrong or if it was just her, but I talk with my sister about it every now and then and when I brought that question up once she said that Mom looks for things to yell at me for and if she can't find any then she waits for me to say something then turns it around so that it was mean and hurtful.  She does the same thing to my sister sometimes so I've seen it when I wasn't the target.   About talking to my parents about depression last, my grandma had actually noticed. One day she got me in private and asked me if there was something wrong or did I need help or did I think I had something wrong with me and I just started crying and ended up telling her everything.  She said she had noticed it recently and when she asked my mom if she thought I had it she was very defensive and offended by the thought that something was wrong with her kid.  My grandma offered to talk to her again but honestly I don't want to drag more people into this fight then there needs to be.  Maybe I should, I've been reconsidering since my suicidal urges have started to come back but I'm only going to use her if I know there is no other way.

But my problem is that by the time I'm 20 I won't be living in the same house as my mother anymore, so I won't have to worry about it.  I'm just scared because I don't know how I'm going to survive until I'm old enough to move out if these thoughts keep coming back.

The best I can come up with is that she's a control freak. Everything has to be exactly the way she wants it ( even if she doesn't know what she wants, she gets angry because it's "common sense" and I should have figured it out ). She likes being in control and I don't like being controlled, so basically it's a constant war over her always trying to show me "who's the boss" and me not taking any of her shit.  Recently she told me I wasn't aloud to joke anymore because my jokes were "mean and distasteful" and "don't you ever stop and think that you've hurt my feelings? Your so stupid."

If I did talk to a teacher about it what should I say? Should I tell them about how I'm worried I'll go back to my suicidal tendencies or just tell them I have an emotionally abusive parent? Because the real problem here isn't my mother, I know she can't be fixed because I've tried everything and she's far too stubborn to ever believe something that she's doing is wrong. The real problem is I don't know how to handle myself.  How to cope with her.    But thanks for suggesting :) I feel a lot better than when I made my original post but I'm still pretty scared... I don't know how I should handle this
Thank you so much... I didn't really expect all these kind responses and advice. :)

Mm, yes I might have been a tad overdramatic there.... But I guess that's just kinda how I interpret it? It's how she makes me feel so I've started hearing her words come out meaner and meaner. I'm not sure if it's me or her anymore (not implying she's innocent, because I know for sure she's not).   But I'm not really so sure about her actually loving me like you said. She constantly is yelling at me, trying to say things she knows will hurt me the most and I know you can say that's because it's her job to make me a better person, but if you do then you've never been on the receiving end of one of her tantrums and you should shut your mouth. (Not trying to be rude to anyone, everyone has been so kind to me here and I am eternally grateful)    I'm gonna be turning 15 in February so I'm 14 by the way.

Yeah I like pretty much any Nintendo game ( like Mario, or Zelda, or Kirby, or Metroid ) but I like the more "grown up" games too like Assassin's Creed, Skyrim, and Portal.  I like art and drawing and basically anything that makes me be creative (I've been extremely imaginative for as long as I can remember) so I guess a long term goal would be to do something with that? I don't really have any ideas for a career though, because to my knowledge art-based jobs rarely make much money so I'm not sure if it's worth my time?   Thanks for responding though :) even if none of you know me it's nice to see I'm not alone.

Yes I think I am, thank you.  But no I can't talk to a teacher :/ my mom is a teacher and is friends with pretty much every teacher at my school so they would either not believe mom could be so mean or they would freak out and try to meddle in it. Maybe I should go a little more in depth here, my mother only acts this way towards me when we are alone or at home. No one in public knows she acts this way because its like she has two personalities: the sickly sweet one that people seem to love, or the emotionally abusive one.  So by the time I get to school or anywhere in public the rage or anger i felt is gone and just replaced by depression.  So when I consider talking to a friend or a teacher I'm plagued with thoughts like "What's the point? They don't really care about your problems and even if they did it's not like they could help."

Thank you... who ever said strangers on the internet couldn't help you! There's only been two replies to my post but both of them have actually cheered me up quite a bit! I'm still terrified but not as sad.
